research_rationale:
EO 10521 (19 FR 1499, signed 1954-03-17) sets out how Federal agencies administer scientific research and assigns the National Science Foundation policy, study and review duties. I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10521.txt). Its number, title, date, signature and filing line (F.R. Doc. 54-2014) agree. Inventory: the dossier's Section 6 span ran through a printed contents page, so I corrected the inventory to 14 spans of the order's own text (Section 6 appears in two parts around the page break). Later events: EO 10807 (24 FR 1897, signed 1959-03-13), section 6(b)(1)-(4), amended the order: it substituted a new Section 1, inserted the word basic in Section 3, edited the ends of Section 8(a) and (b), revoked Section 8(c), and added a new Section 10. Section 6(c) of EO 10807 says the two orders do not limit each other's agencies' functions. EO 10807 itself was later amended and the Council it created was abolished by statute (the OFR table notes Public Law 94-282), but no held source says that this affected the amendments EO 10807 made to EO 10521. The Office of the Federal Register disposition table (jobs/peano-formulario) also lists EO 12608 (1987-09-09) as amending EO 10521. The held text of EO 12608 does not name EO 10521 or any of its subjects; its Section 2 substitutes Office of Management and Budget for Bureau of the Budget in listed orders and in any other order relating to functions delegated to that Office, and the held EO 10521 original contains no such words, so that provision does not change EO 10521 and is not claimed as a later event. Only Section 8(c) ended; every other original clause is claimed operative on 2026-10-14, so the order is claimed in force. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route; I read the coverage of current-law:usc (release point current through 2026-10-09; later laws to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog before selecting them. No held source shows the order or its amendments revoked, superseded or expired, and the order rests on the President's own authority as recited (no statute that could lapse).
